news.title: Somali referee Omar Artan grateful for Super Cup chance after World Cup exclusion
news.lede: Referee was refused entry to US in June. Will take charge of PSG v Aston Villa on Wednesday. The Somali referee Omar Artan, who was refused entry to the US to officiate at the World Cup, has spoken publicly for the first time about the decision and detailed his pride as he prepares to take charge of Wednesday’s Super Cup between Paris Saint-Germain and Aston Villa. Uefa awarded Artan the game days after the 34-year-old was prevented from working at the tournament.

news.title: Barcelona turns down PSG offer for Spanish World Cup hero Ferran Torres – Reports
news.lede: AP AP https://ss-i.thgim.com/public/incoming/ytco5c/article71329410.ece/alternates/FREE_1200/Argentina_Spain_WCup_Soccer_4527_.jpg Julio Cortez Spain's Ferran Torres (7) kisses the trophy after the World Cup final soccer match between Spain and Argentina in East Rutherford, N.J., near New York, Sunday, July 19, 2026. (AP Photo/Julio Cortez) Out of contract with Barca in June 2027, Ferran Torres remained vague about his future in recent interviews he gave during a promotional tour in the United States. Barcelona Barcelona on Monday rejected an initial offer from Paris Saint-Germain estimated at 40 million euros ($46.2 million) for Spanish World Cup winner Ferran Torres, a source within the Catalan club told AFP. “Negotiations are ongoing” between Barca and PSG, the same source added, confirming reports from the daily Mundo Deportivo.

news.title: England stars’ World Cup bomb scare after police dog 'smelled EXPLOSIVES on bus'
news.lede: ENGLAND’S stars were allegedly caught up in a World Cup bomb scare ahead of their semi-final clash against Argentina. A leaked security services’ report, seen by Informacion.es, details a number of terror attempts including the targeting of the Three Lions’ team bus. The horror unfolded before Harry Kane and co suffered a heartbreaking 2-1 defeat to Argentina in Atlanta on July 15, the Spanish outlet said. The shocking documents revealed a police dog handler had marked an area of the England team bus as positive for explosives following claims there was a bomb onboard.

news.title: Training Report: Bayern Munich injured stars almost ready; World Cup contingent out a little longer; and MORE!
news.lede: It has been a busy few days for Bayern Munich when it comes to personnel news. News that emerged on Sunday from Säbener Straße indicated that Bayern Munich stars Alphonso Davies and Jamal Musiala could be back in team training this week (per Bild via @iMiaSanMia): > Among the players currently recovering from injury, Alphonso Davies and Jamal Musiala are the most advanced in their rehab. Both are expected back in team training at the beginning of the coming week [@BILD] In addition, Bild (via @iMiaSanMia) is reporting that Harry Kane, Michael Olise and Dayot Upamecano are getting more time off and will not be fully back in action until next week: > Harry Kane, Michael Olise and Dayot Upamecano have been given more vacation time and won’t return to Munich until the end of the coming week.

news.title: Uefa, Concacaf and AFC push for Infantino to quit and discuss rival competitions
news.lede: Confederations write open letter damning Fifa president. Concacaf president Montagliani seen as top contender. Uefa, the Asian Football Confederation and Concacaf will push for Gianni Infantino to resign after writing an open letter calling for “leadership that serves football, not seeks to command it”. In a dramatic escalation of the war that has threatened to tear football apart since details emerged of the Fifa president’s failed Football Forward Enterprise scheme, the three governing bodies accused Infantino of “trust broken through deception” and condemned his failure to acknowledge that the proposal should not have been unilaterally launched.

news.title: The two Arsenal World Cup stars that cut holiday short as five players return to training
news.lede: The last cluster of Arsenal's World Cup stars were due back at the Sobha Realty Training Centre today, but two players opted to return early on Saturday. Speaking after the Emirates Cup match against Borussia Dortmund, Arteta revealed Bukayo Saka and world champion David Raya were so eager to get cracking they scrapped their final days of rest. Arteta said when asked when the rest of his players would join the group: "Well, some of them were back today, already watching the game. "Some of them, David and Bukayo, were back yesterday, a bit earlier than expected, which is great to see.

news.title: UEFA, AFC, CONCACAF Criticize FIFA Over World Cup Stake Sale
news.lede: Rabat - UEFA , the Asian Football Confederation (AFC), and CONCACAF issued a joint open letter on Monday criticizing FIFA leadership over its handling of a proposed sale of a stake in the commercial rights to the World Cup. The three confederations stopped short of calling for a change in FIFA leadership but accused Infantino of undermining trust through “deception” over the now-abandoned proposal. They also said he had placed himself above the collective interest and called for a fully independent review of the events surrounding the proposal. “Football’s strength has always been its unity.
